I think it's caused by upgrading from 8.12.0-SNAPSHOT, which understands features behind feature flags, to 8.13.0 (non-snapshot release build), which does not.

issue.title: Change CI release tests to not use snapshot versions

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
### Description

**Background**
Currently in CI release tests mix snapshot and release versions. This does not work well when we use feature flags, considering the following:
- enabling and disabling a feature flag is not supported,
- snapshots have the feature flags enabled by default.

**Example**
https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/103365 is an example of a test affected by the above. 
- version `8.12.0-SNAPSHOT` has the feature flag enabled and it writes a new section in the data stream metadata in the cluster state.
- then it upgrades to `8.13.0`, which has the feature flag disabled and crashes because it finds unexpected data in the cluster state.

The test itself can be fixed if we enable the feature flag; however, this means that:
- we are not testing the upgrade paths that our users are experiencing
- when we remove the feature flag and the feature is GA, we might not test the upgrade path when the feature is introduced in the latest version.

**Request**
Since these tests are testing the upgrades, we would like to ask to only use release versions in these tests.

body: Ah sorry for the noise. Can you point me to where you found that exception? I can't seem to find it in the console output.

> This is covered by #103869 - closing.

I don't think that issue will be addressed soon though. The fix here should be to configure the feature flag for these tests. This has been the way we handle flags for _years_ now.
